title: auth/header: clarify project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, request-signing nonce headers (OpenAI compat)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: We have inconsistent header semantics across the API surface and the OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR clarifies and standardizes project vs org keys, introduces scoped tokens for route-level authorization, formalizes a request-signing nonce header for replay protection, and tightens CORS behavior for browser clients. Changes are implemented in the API gateway, openai-compat shim, and docs. Checklist: 1) Define header semantics and precedence (X-Redwood-Project vs Authorization Bearer project::token) 2) Add scoped token support and validation logic 3) Add X-Redwood-Nonce for request-signing and replay detection 4) Update CORS defaults to disallow credentialed requests from unknown origins and add documented opt-in for browser SDKs 5) OpenAI-compat mapping for OpenAI-Organization/OpenAI-Api-Key 6) Update SDKs and docs and add conformance tests. This description is a single continuous string containing motivation, checklist, and rollout notes. Rollout notes: we add feature-flag control and a compatibility mode for 30 days. We emit deprecation warnings in logs when legacy X-Project-Id header is used.

release_notes:
- Standardize header semantics: Authorization Bearer tokens, X-Redwood-Project takes precedence for project-scoped requests
- Introduce scoped tokens for route-level authorization and better least-privilege controls
- Add X-Redwood-Nonce header to support request-signing and replay protection
- OpenAI-compat: map OpenAI-Organization/OpenAI-Api-Key to internal org/project model
- CORS: tightened defaults for browser clients; opt-in path for SDK/browser use
- Deprecated legacy X-Project-Id header (30-day compatibility window with deprecation warnings)
notes: Feature gated rollout: default compatibility mode enabled for 30 days then switch to strict mode. Operational playbook updated to monitor auth failures and CORS denials. Added metrics: auth.header.legacy_usage, auth.nonce.replays, auth.scoped_token.invalid_attempts. Backwards compatibility: openai-compat shim accepts both old and new header patterns during transition.
